posts.cooked:
I would completely take it at that cost.  We have enough of both to provide huge replayability, and repeating the same 12 environments over and over is getting incredibly tedious.  They don't even begin to suggest all the places a battle can happen.

What would be really nice would be if there was a set of "generic" environment decks where you shuffle two of them together to create an environment.  Say "Jungle", "desert", "ocean", "ruins", "creatures", "storm".  One of the first three plus one of the second three...nine combinations.  "desert ruins" and "ocean ruins" would be like Anubis and Atlantis respectively, while "desert creatures" might be the Final Wasteland, but that'd still be three new environments we don't have, and a quadratic potential for more.

posts.cooked: When I first started playing this game, I thought more generic environments would be great (in fact, I made a handful and posted them to my site).  But as things have progressed, I've found I really enjoy the specific nature of the environments.  It's a subtle difference, but I think it would be less interesting to play in a generic Egyptian tomb or floating villain fortress.  I like playing in one that's tied so closely to the story going on in my head.

posts.name: UXM266
posts.cooked:
It seems that my points weren't explained clearly, and I will do my best to give my best explanation. It might be long but hopefully it works.

Though there seems to be a lot of villains, ESPECIALLY on Spider-Man and Batman's side, there are more heroes. I am not counting the X-Men, the Avengers and the justice League as one hero. But how many Teen Titan's, Mutants, Avengers, and JL members are there?

One of the biggest problems in comics now is trying to introduce new characters, and places. For the most part they don't fare well. They either get called redundant for being too similar to something else, such as a teenage-this, or a female-version-that, or these-IN-SPACE, or those-but-alternate-uiverse.

You can't add a new location simply because it's new. It has to be different enough to be interesting, but not too crazy that it's kitschy. 

The good thing about having only a set few of tools is that writers and artists don't need to constantly create, new worlds, and explain what they are to the heroes, why they should be there, how they got there and what it is. Doing something new without explaining WHY or HOW is a risky move in the comic book industry.

In relation to SOTM? I like the way the things are numbered. H>V>E
